title: Portability: projection and copied-project shadow matrix
description: Objective: exercise the shipped legacy importer, task-80fce1d1d625453098bd526d61c5ddb8's real daemon shadow adapter, and public compareShadowProjections over a copied-project corpus. Produce exact PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN advisory outcomes while proving the source copy and durable current store remain byte-for-byte untouched.
definitionOfDone: A nonempty copied-project corpus is read through the production legacy importer and compared with the production daemon shadow adapter at one captured store horizon; the test never constructs the current ShadowProjection itself.

Generated matched, changed, absent-current, absent-legacy, unmapped-field, malformed, and unreadable cases assert a positive case count plus the exact mismatch kind/disposition or stable refusal code/layer; one full exact-match control yields zero mismatches.
Every case records the checkout source commit and canonical fixture manifest digest, and repeated runs over unchanged bytes produce identical ordered comparison bytes.
Before/after SHA-256, file-size, and mtime inventories for the copied corpus plus raw SQLite event/decision counts and database bytes/mtime are identical, including every refusal arm.
Focused integration tests execute with nonzero test counts on Windows and use native temp/path handling that is portable to Linux and macOS.
taskRails: Use only public package roots and the real production surface under test; no test helper may reimplement a projection, provider decision, transport handshake, or host adapter.
Every refusal/failure arm asserts the exact stable reason code and refusing layer; generated matrices assert a positive case count and include an accepted control so refusal-only suites cannot pass.
All fixtures and results are advisory/read-only: no imported state may activate, mutate durable authority, select a best tool, or perform cutover.
Use TDD and mutation-drill the production surface so a named assertion reddens; keep owned files focused and stage/commit only explicit paths.
Hard-depend on task-80fce1d1d625453098bd526d61c5ddb8; missing LINK/BLOCKER authority must remain UNKNOWN/refused, never filled by fixture assumptions.
Own only the projection matrix test and at most two focused fixture/helper files under tests/integration/portability.

implementationPlan.description:
THE CORPUS: create tests/integration/portability/shadow-corpus-fixtures.ts (helper 1 of the 2 task rail 6 permits).
It declares a NONEMPTY copied-project corpus as data plus the case table, and contains no assertions and no store access.
- CORPUS: legacy source records covering at least a claim with links, a claim with `links: []`, a HISTORICAL claim and a SUSPENDED claim. The last two matter because the daemon mapper emits a BLOCKER only for SUSPENDED, and `links: []` is KNOWN-EMPTY rather than unavailable — that distinction is the semantic hinge of the whole adapter and a corpus that never exercises it cannot see a regression in it.
- MATERIALISATION: write the corpus to a temp directory as real files, so `buildSourceManifest` and `decodeLegacySources` walk bytes on disk exactly as they would for a real copied project. A corpus held only in memory would skip the manifest digest this task must record.
- CASE TABLE: one row per DoD-2 case — matched, changed, absent-current, absent-legacy, unmapped-field, malformed, unreadable — each declaring its expected mismatch kind and disposition, or its expected refusal code AND refusing layer. Import `SHADOW_MISMATCH_KINDS`, `SHADOW_MISMATCH_DISPOSITIONS` and `SHADOW_ENTITY_FIELDS` from the @moe/import root and `IMPORT_SHADOW_REFUSAL_CODES` / `IMPORT_SHADOW_READ_LAYER` from the @moe/daemon root rather than spelling any of them locally; a locally spelled code is a second vocabulary that drifts, and the drift shows up as a green test asserting something production no longer emits.
- Export the case count so step 4 can assert it is POSITIVE before running anything.

THE HARNESS: create tests/integration/portability/shadow-corpus-harness.ts (helper 2 of 2). Lifecycle and evidence capture only — no assertions, no expected values, no projection logic.
- COPY AND INVENTORY: copy the corpus into `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "moe-shadow-"))` and capture a BEFORE inventory for every corpus file: SHA-256, byte size and mtime. Provide the same capture as an AFTER call. Digest AND size AND mtime for EVERY entry, never a sample — a write that restores identical content still moves mtime, and that is the point.
- REAL STORE: `SqliteEventStore.openForProject(dbPath, projectId)`. NOT `open`: a handle opened without a project refuses every commit with PROJECT_SCOPE_REQUIRED, which the neighbouring tests/integration/import suite already documents. Capture raw event count, command-decision count, database file size and mtime, before and after.
- PRODUCTION INGEST: a helper that takes a corpus directory and runs the PRODUCTION chain — `buildSourceManifest` -> `decodeLegacySources` -> `applyImport` -> `commitLegacyImport` — returning the manifest digest and the `LegacyImportFacts` the importer derived. Nothing here may hand-build an `ImportCommitInput` or an event payload; the byte-identity claim is about what the importer drafted.
- TEARDOWN in a `finally` on every path: close every store, remove every temp root. A held SQLite handle kills the vitest worker with an error that looks unrelated to the test.
- Native path handling throughout (`join`, `tmpdir`), so the suite is portable to Linux and macOS while being exercised on Windows (DoD item 5).

THE ACCEPTED CONTROL, first, in tests/integration/portability/projection-shadow-matrix.test.ts.
Before any case runs, assert the generated case count is POSITIVE and that every declared case kind appears at least once — a generated matrix that silently produces zero cases passes while testing nothing, which is why the epic rail names it explicitly.
Then the full exact-match control required by DoD item 2: ingest the whole corpus through the production chain, then call `compareImportShadow(store, { manifestDigest }, legacyFacts)` from the @moe/daemon root with the SAME facts the importer derived. Assert `comparison.mismatches` is EMPTY and `comparison.refusals` is empty.
THE TEST MUST NEVER CONSTRUCT THE CURRENT PROJECTION (DoD item 1, task rail 1). It never calls `projectLegacyImport` for the current side, never assembles a `ShadowProjection` literal, and never substitutes BoardProjection or WorkClaimLedger. `compareImportShadow` reads the current side itself through `readImportShadowProjection` at one captured horizon; the suite's only job is to supply the legacy facts and read the verdict.
This control is what keeps every refusal case below honest: a refusal-only suite where nothing can ever match would report every refusal correctly and still prove nothing (task rail 2).

THE MISMATCH ARMS — DoD item 2's generated matched/changed/absent-current/absent-legacy/unmapped-field cases, each asserting the EXACT mismatch kind AND its disposition, read from `SHADOW_MISMATCH_DISPOSITIONS` rather than hand-asserted.
- CHANGED: alter one CLAIM field on the LEGACY side only (principal or status) -> `FIELD_DIFFERS` / NEEDS_RECONCILIATION, with `legacyValue` and `currentValue` both populated and different.
- ABSENT-CURRENT: commit a SUBSET of the corpus durably, then compare against the FULL legacy facts -> `ENTITY_ABSENT_ON_CURRENT` / NEEDS_RECONCILIATION for the uncommitted entity. This is the arm that proves the current side really came from durable rows: if the suite were building the current projection itself, the entity could not be missing.
- ABSENT-LEGACY: the mirror — compare a reduced legacy fact set against the fully committed store -> `ENTITY_ABSENT_ON_LEGACY` / UNKNOWN. Note the asymmetry is deliberate in the contract: a fact only the new side has is UNKNOWN to this comparison, not a legacy defect, and asserting the disposition is what pins that.
- UNMAPPED-FIELD: a legacy field outside `SHADOW_ENTITY_FIELDS` -> `FIELD_UNMAPPED` / UNKNOWN, and assert `comparison.refusals` carries ONE typed refusal for it with its exact code and layer. The contract promises one typed refusal per unmapped field precisely so the code is never inferred.
- KNOWN-EMPTY IS NOT A MISMATCH: the `links: []` claim and the HISTORICAL claim must produce ZERO LINK and ZERO BLOCKER mismatches and zero refusals. Collapsing known-empty into unavailable is how a shadow comparison starts inventing or hiding reconciliation work; assert the absence as a fact.

DETERMINISM AND PROVENANCE — DoD item 3.
- SOURCE COMMIT: capture `git rev-parse HEAD` ONCE at suite start and record it on every case result. Assert every case carries that same commit; a matrix whose halves ran against different trees is comparing two systems.
- FIXTURE MANIFEST DIGEST: record the canonical manifest digest `buildSourceManifest` derived for the corpus on every case, and assert it is stable across cases that share a corpus. The digest is the importer's own, never recomputed here — recomputing it would be a second derivation that can disagree with the one the events were committed under.
- IDENTICAL ORDERED BYTES: run the entire matrix twice over unchanged corpus bytes in one process and assert the ordered comparison output serializes byte-identically. The comparator has no clock and no random source and its mismatch order is total, so any instability is a real defect rather than expected noise. If some field is genuinely environment-dependent, exclude it BY NAME with a comment — never by comparing a subset, which passes every gate while proving nothing.
- Also assert the two runs produced the same number of mismatches per case, so a difference cannot hide inside a serialization that happens to sort equal.

THE UNTOUCHED-BYTES PROOF — DoD item 4, and the claim the task title is really about.
Assert on BYTES rather than on promises, for the copied corpus and for the durable store, across EVERY arm including refusals:
- CORPUS: the AFTER inventory equals the BEFORE inventory entry-for-entry — SHA-256, size and mtime for every file. Include the mtime deliberately: an accidental write-mode open that restores identical content still moves it, and that is the only signal of it.
- STORE: raw event count, command-decision count, database file size and database mtime unchanged across every read and every comparison. `ImportShadowStorePort` declares only two readers, so a write is not merely unexpected — it is unrepresentable through the port the adapter holds; assert it anyway, because the suite hands the adapter a REAL store and the guarantee is about what the adapter does with it.
- ADVISORY POSTURE (task rail 3): assert every accepted result carries `advisoryOnly: true` and `authority: "NONE"` on BOTH arms as the contract promises, and that nothing in the matrix activates imported state, selects a best tool, or performs a cutover. Assert the returned object exposes no method that could.
- Prove the inventory itself can fail: as a positive control, deliberately touch one corpus file in a scratch copy and confirm the comparison reports it. An inventory that cannot detect a change is a green light wired to nothing.

MUTATION DRILLS against the PRODUCTION surface (task rail 4). Run each, record the exact test name that reddened, restore, and confirm the restored bytes hash-match the original — git status alone is unreliable in this shared worktree, where a foreign hook commit can swallow a drill.
1. THE TAUTOLOGY DRILL, most important: in `apps/daemon/src/projections/import-shadow-reader.ts`, make `compareImportShadow` derive the CURRENT side from `projectLegacyImport(legacyFacts)` instead of from `readImportShadowProjection`. The CHANGED and ABSENT-CURRENT cases must redden. If they stay green, this matrix is comparing one function with itself and every future "agreement" it reports is meaningless.
2. In `apps/daemon/src/projections/import-shadow-mapper.ts`, drop `sourcePath` from the CLAIM fields. The exact-match control must redden with a FIELD_ABSENT mismatch — proving the control is comparing real field sets rather than counting entities.
3. Emit a BLOCKER for the HISTORICAL claim as well as the SUSPENDED one. The known-empty assertion must redden.
4. Remove the `IMPORT_SHADOW_ABSENT` branch so an empty aggregate falls through. The absent-aggregate test must redden ON THE CODE, not on a generic failure.
5. Delete the horizon re-read so drift goes unnoticed. The horizon-drift test must redden.
Restore every production file afterwards; none is an owned path of this task and none may appear in the final diff.

GATE. tests/integration is typechecked by NOTHING in this repo: the root `typecheck` script is `pnpm --recursive typecheck` over workspace packages, and `test:integration` runs only `pnpm typecheck:packaging` (tools/packaging) before vitest. A type error in these three files is invisible to every existing gate. Compensate explicitly and RECORD the command, since no script would show it ran: `npx tsc --noEmit` over the three new files with the same flag set `typecheck:packaging` uses (strict, module nodenext, moduleResolution nodenext, verbatimModuleSyntax), EXIT=0 required.
Then run the suite FROM POWERSHELL — `pnpm test:integration` shells through MSYS tar and fails on drive-letter paths under Git Bash for reasons unrelated to this diff. Capture exit codes separately; no pipes (a piped run reports the pipe tail's code) and no `&&` chaining (a red leg then hides the count line). READ THE OUTPUT: the focused leg `vitest run tests/integration/portability` must print a `Test Files N passed` count line with a NONZERO count — a path filter matching nothing exits 0 with no count line at all.
Run the suite TWICE in a row in one command: a teardown that has only ever run once has not been tested, and this suite creates temp trees, real SQLite files and inventories on every case.
Then attribute any red by the path-attributed baseline: repo-wide failures at the merge-base, again at HEAD, and confirm the delta intersected with this task's three owned paths is EMPTY. Report foreign red verbatim with exact failing paths; never hide it and never fabricate green. Expect peer churn in this directory — task-efe5465f owns three other files here.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, then complete. Load the `adversarial-self-review` skill and read the diff as an attacker:
- Does any line construct a `ShadowProjection`, call `projectLegacyImport` for the CURRENT side, or reach BoardProjection / WorkClaimLedger? Grep for all three. DoD item 1 and task rail 1 both forbid it, and it is the single easiest way for this matrix to become self-confirming.
- Is every SURFACE UNDER TEST reached by bare specifier (@moe/daemon, @moe/import, @moe/store)? The only permitted relative reach is `tools/import/*`, which cannot have a bare specifier because tools/ is not a workspace package — name that exception explicitly in the notes.
- Did any refusal arm assert only `ok === false` without pinning the layer?
- Did any arm leave a temp tree, a SQLite handle, or a modified corpus behind? The AFTER inventory should have caught a modified corpus — confirm the inventory positive control actually fails when it should.
- Are all expected codes and dispositions imported from their owning package roots rather than spelled locally?
COMPLETION MUST RECORD, per the acceptance rail: the certified capability is the daemon shadow adapter `compareImportShadow` / `readImportShadowProjection`, shipped by task-80fce1d1d625453098bd526d61c5ddb8 and verified on disk in step 1; the durable current-side rows come from the production writer `commitLegacyImport` shipped by task-6d319381967a4ca5b746c2538f537e72, which CLOSES the vacuous-green hazard the reopen note carried forward — state whether it was present at execution time, since the plan assumed it. Also record the generated case count and the corpus manifest digest.
Stage and commit ONLY the three owned paths by explicit pathspec; never `git add -A`, and confirm the step-9 drill edits under apps/daemon are fully restored and absent from the diff.
